description: Meal-parsing cases for /api/parse, each with a reference calorie range assembled from standard food-composition data. The ranges are deliberately wide: portions in a free-text description are approximate, so a narrow 'ground truth' would be false precision.
sources: USDA FoodData Central (fdc.nal.usda.gov), SR Legacy and Foundation Foods
IFCT 2017, Indian Food Composition Tables (NIN Hyderabad)
Label values for packaged items (soft drinks, pizza) where composition varies by brand
notes: kcal is per portion as described in the text, in kilocalories.
match lists the name fragments that identify this item in whatever the model returns, so a model that splits '2 rotis' into two rows is still credited correctly.
Where a description leaves cooking fat ambiguous, the range assumes a plain preparation and the basis says so.

cases.text: 2 rotis, dal, and a glass of lassi
cases.basis: A 45 g whole-wheat roti is ~100-130 kcal; a katori (150 g) of cooked toor dal is ~120-180 kcal; a 250 ml glass of sweet lassi is ~120-200 kcal.

cases.text: leftover rice with two eggs and half a bell pepper
cases.basis: One cup (158 g) of cooked white rice is ~205 kcal; two large eggs are ~143 kcal; half a bell pepper is ~15 kcal. Plain preparation, no added fat.

cases.text: 100g grilled chicken breast, a cup of cooked white rice, and a cup of broccoli
cases.basis: 100 g of grilled skinless chicken breast is ~165 kcal; one cup of cooked white rice is ~205 kcal; one cup of cooked broccoli is ~55 kcal.

cases.text: a three-egg cheese omelette with two slices of buttered toast
cases.basis: Three eggs are ~215 kcal, 30 g of cheese ~110 kcal and the cooking butter ~35 kcal; two slices of white toast are ~160 kcal plus ~70 kcal of butter. A model is free to answer with one omelette row or with separate egg and cheese rows, so both spellings are accepted and the rows are summed.
One cup (158 g) of cooked white rice is ~205 kcal and two large eggs are ~143 kcal, for ~350 kcal plain. This is the case the model was suspected of scoring at 245-320 kcal.

A restaurant plate of chicken biryani (roughly 350-450 g with a piece of chicken) is ~450-750 kcal depending on the rice-to-meat ratio and the ghee used. The wide range is the point: one 'plate' is not a measurement.

cases.text: a masala dosa with coconut chutney
cases.basis: A restaurant masala dosa with potato filling is ~250-400 kcal; a small bowl (50 g) of coconut chutney is ~40-90 kcal.

cases.text: a bowl of oatmeal with milk and a spoon of honey
cases.basis: 40 g of dry rolled oats is ~150 kcal; 150 ml of semi-skimmed milk is ~70 kcal; a teaspoon of honey is ~20 kcal, a tablespoon ~60 kcal, so the range covers both readings.
A medium banana (118 g edible) is ~105 kcal.

cases.text: two samosas and a cup of masala chai
cases.basis: A fried potato-and-pea samosa (60-80 g) is ~125-200 kcal depending on the pastry and the oil absorbed; a 150 ml cup of masala chai with milk and sugar is ~60-130 kcal.
A slice of takeaway pepperoni pizza (roughly 110 g) is ~250-350 kcal, so two slices are ~500-700 kcal. Thin-crust slices sit at the bottom of that range.

cases.text: black coffee with two teaspoons of sugar
cases.basis: Black coffee is ~2-5 kcal; two level teaspoons of sugar (8 g) are ~32 kcal. A small number on purpose: near-zero items are where percentage error stops meaning anything.
Not a food. The service is expected to refuse rather than invent a meal, so this case has no calorie reference and passes only when the request is rejected.
